overall: Atlanta is running significantly hotter than expected this morning, with the observed running max of 84.2°F at 11:05 ET already surpassing all three NWP model TMAX forecasts. The warming trend is active with a strong short-term velocity of +3.6°F/hr, though the 2-hour velocity of +1.8°F/hr and persistent broken overcast (100% cloud fraction, ceiling only ~2,300 ft) suggest the pace of heating may moderate through the afternoon. The high dewpoint of 73.4°F reflects a humid air mass that, while adding to the heat load, also tends to limit peak surface heating under cloud cover.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models (ECMWF 81.3°F, HRRR 82.1°F, NBM 81.0°F) have already been busted by observed conditions — the running max at 11:05 AM has cleared all three by at least 2°F. max_temp_prediction: With 84.2°F already locked in as the running max and the timing model pointing to a peak near 2:18 PM, additional warming of 3–5°F is plausible if cloud cover partially breaks or solar angle sustains the current heating rate. The META model concentrates probability mass across 84–89°F (roughly 68% combined) with a median near 87–88°F, while the observation-driven intraday model leans more bullish toward 90–91°F; balancing these against the inhibiting effect of the thick low overcast, a final high near 88°F appears most likely with meaningful upside risk toward 90°F if clouds thin. Confidence is moderate — the already-busted NWP guidance and active timing uncertainty add meaningful spread.
